title: Scenarios in courses: ideas from other products
intro: This page gathers ideas for adding reusable scenarios to a course inside Courses in Essentials 2.0. It looks at how instructors pick items from institutional and personal libraries, place them in a course, and manage order and course-specific settings. Screenshots come from the design reference libraries Mobbin and Refero. Scenario authoring is out of scope. Events, competencies, learner visibility and Canvas hand-off sit in neighbouring areas.

questions.title: How do people search, filter and preview a library before adding an item?
questions.answer: Figma separates finding a reusable item from inspecting and inserting it. Assets search and library filters lead to a Details preview with source info and 'Insert instance' (Figma assets flow; Figma details preview). Canva keeps a large preview visible while options change (Canva template preview). MasterClass has compact category and filter discovery, but for learners rather than authors (MasterClass lesson library). For Essentials, combine searchable institutional and own libraries with optional scenario inspection and a selection list that stays as people browse. Filters for competency, duration and equipment are ideas for our product; this set does not show them together.

questions.title: Can people select several items and add them together, or only one at a time?
questions.answer: Teachable imports checked lessons from a source course into a destination curriculum (Teachable import). PandaDoc makes the batch clear with 'Add 2 items' and confirms insertion in the document (PandaDoc content library). Canva offers a single-design 'Copy to course' or 'Move' choice (Canva copy to course). Circle's one-question authoring flow is an example of what not to do for this reuse task (Circle add question). Essentials should let instructors select several known scenarios, review a count, and add them once into a chosen section.

questions.title: When you add a library item, is it a copy or a link: do later edits to the original reach the course, and can the course change its own settings?
questions.answer: Figma inserts a linked copy of a library item, names its source and lets you pick which set of variables to use (Figma insert instance). Ditto attaches selected text to a named library component and confirms the link (Ditto attach). Notion shows 'Synced block', and Canva shows a choose-then-edit path into the editor; neither screenshot set shows later sync (Notion synced block; Canva template path). None of these screenshots show whether later changes to the original reach the course, or whether course overrides survive. Essentials needs a clear decision on a linked version, a fixed copy and course-only settings before writing the wording on screen.

questions.title: After items are added, how do people reorder them, group them into sections and set prerequisites?
questions.answer: Circle shows before and after moving a whole section while keeping its lessons and Draft labels (Circle section reorder). Kajabi makes grouped content visible along with Draft, Publish, 'Drip' and 'Lock' labels. Podia shows a delayed section; Teachable shows section release by date or days after enrollment (Kajabi outline; Podia delayed section; Teachable drip). The screenshots support grouping and sequence management in place. They do not show setup of prerequisites between items. Keep sequence separate from event scheduling and learner release.

questions.title: Which details (competencies, duration, equipment) come along with an item and show in the course outline?
questions.answer: Mindvalley, MasterClass and Udemy keep activity titles, numbering and duration in learner outlines (Mindvalley program detail; MasterClass outline; Udemy lecture list). That supports a scannable outline, but none of the screenshots show an instructor copying those details from an original library item. For Essentials, duration, competencies and equipment could appear as fields on each course row; where they come from, who can edit them and what learners see are still design decisions. Event links should open the Events area rather than imply that adding a scenario schedules it.

questions.title: What does a new, empty course show, and how are suggestions offered?
questions.answer: Podia eases the first empty course with light guidance and example content; Kajabi shows an editable starter outline (Podia course builder; Kajabi generated outline). Teachable offers outline methods and an explained empty course list (Teachable outline methods; Teachable empty courses). Circle shows an empty section with add buttons on the same screen but no library path (Circle empty lessons). Essentials should open with 'Browse scenario library', optional suggested scenarios and clear empty and no-results screens. MasterClass's no-results message sits beside an unrelated course card, so what the search found is unclear (MasterClass no-results). Suggested items should stay editable and should not silently become scheduled learner activities.

references.title: Template preview with live options
references.question: Q1
references.take: Suggested templates stay visible beside a live preview and Use Canva Editor. Search, filters and course-add are not on this screen.

references.title: Asset library search and filters
references.question: Q1
references.take: Figma shows an Assets panel with a search field, shared-library toggles, and grid or list layout controls before insertion.

references.title: Component details before insert
references.question: Q1
references.take: Figma opens a focused details pop-up so you can inspect a reusable review-card component before placing it on the canvas.

references.title: Browse a filtered lesson library
references.question: Q1
references.take: The library shows search, category filters, Filters and Clear filters, and lesson rows by category. This is learner discovery; there is no author add action.

references.title: Create and publish a course
references.question: Q1
references.take: Shows an empty course list and a guided create-course flow, not reusable-library browsing or scenario preview and add.

references.title: Copy a design into a course
references.question: Q2
references.take: Choose design searches existing work, offers Copy to course or Move, and returns the copied item to Activities. Only one design can be selected.

references.title: Add quiz questions one at a time
references.question: Q2
references.take: Add question sets up and saves one original quiz question in a pop-up window. No library, multi-select or batch add is visible.

references.title: Select and batch-add library items
references.question: Q2
references.take: A searchable Content Library supports several selected cards, Deselect all, an Add 2 items action that names the count, and immediate insertion of both blocks.

references.title: Import selected lessons from another course
references.question: Q2
references.take: Import content picks a source course and shows row and section checkboxes plus Select all and none. It imports several lessons in one action, then shows them in Curriculum with a short confirmation message.

references.title: Build a quiz inside a lesson
references.question: Q2
references.take: The quiz builder edits one question and its answers on the same screen, then offers New question. Useful as an authoring example of what not to do for reusable-library batch selection.

references.title: Edit a chosen template copy
references.question: Q3
references.take: An AI request, three generated choices, a selected design, a Color control and Use Canva Editor suggest choose-then-edit copy behaviour. No source link, later updates to the original or overrides are shown. Possible example of what not to do.

references.title: Attach text to a library component
references.question: Q3
references.take: Select text, open Library, Attach to existing component, pick the matching hero-title, then Attach. A linked label and confirmation message appear. The screenshots do not show later changes to the original or overrides.

references.title: Insert and set up a linked library item
references.question: Q3
references.take: Browse library, open Cards, open Review Card details, choose 'Insert instance', pick which variables to use, then place the card. The selected item names Review Card and the Simple Design System source. The screenshots do not show whether later changes to the original reach the course, or whether overrides survive.

references.title: Insert a synced block from the menu
references.question: Q3
references.take: Advanced blocks offers Synced block as an insertion choice. The created block, source identity, edits, update spread and overrides are not shown.

references.title: Reorder lessons and sections in a course
references.question: Q4
references.take: Five frames show a new fifth lesson, then the whole Culinary Explorations section lifted above The World of Potatoes, still holding its lessons and Draft states.

references.title: Outline with modules, statuses and add content
references.question: Q4
references.take: One authoring screen shows four grouped modules, Add Content controls, collapse controls, and Draft, Publish, 'Drip' and 'Lock' labels. No reorder action or prerequisite setup is shown.

references.title: Lessons grouped in sections with delay
references.question: Q4
references.take: The authoring screen shows New lesson and New section, lessons grouped in sections, and a module labeled Delayed 1 day. No reorder action or item prerequisite is shown.

references.title: Curriculum with sections and release timing
references.question: Q4
references.take: A sectioned curriculum shows lesson rows and creation controls. An open Drip panel sets release by date or days after enrollment. Grip icons are visible, but movement is not shown.

references.title: Curriculum in numbered sections
references.question: Q4
references.take: The learner view shows 14 sections, 88 lectures, numbered lessons in an expanded first section, and later sections collapsed. Authoring, reorder and prerequisite controls are absent.

references.title: Outline with numbered sections and duration
references.question: Q5
references.take: The desktop learner outline shows numbered sections and an expanded activity with sequence, thumbnail, title, description and a 5-minute duration.

references.title: Mobile curriculum with duration
references.question: Q5
references.take: The mobile curriculum shows numbered sections and expanded activity cards with sequence, thumbnail, title and a 4-minute estimate where supplied.

references.title: Program detail with counts and durations
references.question: Q5
references.take: Program detail shows 29 lessons and 11h 34m. The Lessons view shows minutes per item, and a resource card shows type plus a 5-minute duration. Automatic copying from a source into the outline is not shown.

references.title: AI-assisted course outline workspace
references.question: Q5
references.take: Outline creation asks for a course title and student-facing description and offers AI generation. No curriculum item details or transfer is visible.

references.title: Lecture list with durations and downloads
references.question: Q5
references.take: The learner lecture outline keeps section, lesson number, media type, title, remaining duration and a download control together.

references.title: Empty lessons with add buttons
references.question: Q6
references.take: Shows 1 section, 0 lessons, an editable Untitled section - 1, Add new and Add section on the same screen. No suggestions, examples, guidance or library path.

references.title: Starter outline with search and add content
references.question: Q6
references.take: Confirms successful outline creation, then shows search, three populated modules, global and module Add content actions, expandable rows and Draft controls. Generation itself is not shown.

references.title: Search with a no-results message
references.question: Q6
references.take: Reports No results found for 'buddism' while category controls, filters and an unrelated Terence Tao course card stay visible, so what the search found is unclear. Example of what not to do.

references.title: Course builder with guidance and starter outline
references.question: Q6
references.take: Combines How to create an online course and See how guidance, New lesson and New section actions, and starter content with sample text, video and quiz lessons.

references.title: Course creation from an empty list
references.question: Q6
references.take: An empty Courses table explains where new courses will appear and offers 'Create course' and 'Learn more'. Only the first screen of this sequence was collected, so what comes next is not shown.

references.title: Choose a course outline method
references.question: Q6
references.take: On the last of five setup steps ('Step 5/5'), Teachable offers three ways to build the course outline: 'Generate with AI' from a description, 'Start from scratch' and 'Bulk upload'. 'Back' and 'Finish' buttons sit below.
